discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with WMAP, establishing the standard cosmological model

nominees.name: David N. Spergel
nominees.affiliation: Simons Foundation and Princeton University, USA

motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe, conceived and led by Charles Bennett with Lyman Page directing its instrument and calibration and David Spergel leading its theoretical interpretation, turned cosmology into a precision physical science. Its carefully calibrated, differential full-sky maps measured the temperature and polarization anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background with unprecedented fidelity. From them, the team determined the age, geometry and composition of the universe to percent-level accuracy. They established a flat universe dominated by dark energy and cold dark matter, and found nearly scale-invariant primordial fluctuations consistent with inflation. They also dated cosmic reionization, the epoch whose first galaxies JWST now observes directly. WMAP is a model of what patient instrument-building combined with rigorous analysis can achieve: a new observational window that defined the framework within which all modern cosmology, from Planck to JWST deep fields, is interpreted.
